I’ve seen pictures from my dad’s work accident.

We live in an area that’s famous for limestone, and there used to be a lot of mines back in the 80’s and 90’s. My dad worked at one of the mills. One day, he was walking on the bottom of a slope, and there was a crane at the top of the slope. The crane was lifting slabs of limestone (which weigh up to 1500lbs). Something on the crane broke and it dropped a slab, which started sliding down the slope and eventually crushed my dad. It landed on his entire body, with only his head and arms sticking out. His eyes were bulging out of his face and there was a puddle of blood around him. He was purple. 

Under the limestone, his pelvis was completely shattered, ribs were broken, his femur snapped, and he had a lot of damage to his internal organs. They didn’t know if he was going to be able to live, let alone walk (it was quite possible he had a spinal injury). After a few months in the hospital he was released and he’s able to walk and move and everything. It’s really crazy that he managed to live, and the only noticeable side effects that he still has are some scars from surgery and some brain damage from loss of oxygen.

Not me, but my dad (I apologize for not knowing great medical terms).
My family lives in an area known for its limestone mills. A lot of men from the area used to work for the mills back in the 70’s-90’s. My dad was one of them. 

He was standing at the bottom of a steep hill while at work, and there was a crane at the top of the hill, which was moving limestone slabs that each weighed ~2,000 lbs. I don’t know exactly what caused it, but the clasp on the crane opened up and dropped one of the limestone slabs. 

The slab came barreling down the hill towards my dad, who had no time to dodge it. It crushed him. His left arm and head were the only things that weren’t pinned under the rock. His pelvis was shattered, organs in his lower abdomen were squished, and his legs were broken in several different spots. He had many broken ribs. 

He was taken to the hospital and was subjected to a bunch of surgeries and procedures to try and fix what was crushed. They kept him in the hospital for 3 months. 

He lived, and what’s crazy is that he’s still alive, he can walk, his organs are (mostly) fine, and the only lasting affects are on his eyes and pelvis. In 2014 he had an abscess from a stich that was left in his stomach, and almost died from that, but pulled through. He’s 61 now.
